category_title: Reluctant stayers who use inappropriate language and avoid academic tasks
minimal_context: The student is participating in a whole-class discussion about numeracy applications using an overhead projector.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's look at the numeracy applications on the overhead projector. Please work through the first question on your worksheet.

STUDENT: I'm not on the planet today, mate. Did anyone watch the game last night?

TUTOR: We need to get through these questions.

STUDENT: I'm not doing the work. I'm just not well, cross and cranky.

TUTOR: Please stop talking and look at the slide.

STUDENT: Mate, I don't want to have to get angry the first day. Too much talking anyway, I'm not doing this.

options.A: Make explicit moves acknowledging and praising appropriate student behaviors (e.g., "I'm impressed. Go you good things. It's awesome to see your focus.").
options.B: Ask probing questions about the numeracy applications on the overhead projector, such as "What are you checking to see?" and "How many parts fit?"
options.C: Simplify the instructions for the worksheet questions during the whole-class discussion about the numeracy applications.
options.D: Keep a kit comprising assorted coloring sheets, art materials, and crayons available for the student during the numeracy lesson.
